source.title: Doubly infinite residual neural networks: a diffusion process approach

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies residual-network propagation and training, but does not report training classification error or test a claim version's stated outcome.
record.gate_note: The MNIST experiments report test accuracy, not training classification error. The paper also reports theoretical propagation and kernel results; these do not measure the outcomes named in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study reports initialization-time signal propagation, Jacobian and kernel properties, and final MNIST test accuracy. It does not measure training error, training speed, learning-rate stability thresholds, or the initialization and architectural comparisons specified by V1–V6. Well-behaved Jacobians alone do not establish faster learning or greater trainable depth.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. Under smoothness, depth-scaling and non-explosivity assumptions, the authors establish well-behaved propagation for infinitely deep identity ResNets. For a restricted i.i.d. fully connected architecture, they derive simple doubly infinite kernels; equivalence of full training to linear regression additionally assumes control of NTK fluctuations during training. Some doubly infinite derivations are heuristic. MNIST test-accuracy experiments support the predicted GD/SGD limit, while mini-batch Adam escapes this behavior within tested sizes and Adam performs better for large convolutional models.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes depth-scaled residual-network initialization and reports MNIST test-accuracy experiments; it does not use the claim versions' CIFAR training-classification-error recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different behavior for GD/SGD and Adam as model size grows: Adam is described as escaping the linear-model solution domain and performing better at large sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully connected ResNet final MNIST test accuracy approaches the linear-regression reference under GD and SGD; mini-batch Adam departs from this behavior. For convolutional ResNets, Adam gives superior test accuracy at large joint width and depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these depth-scaled tanh ResNets, final MNIST test accuracy depends on optimizer and joint width/depth, with GD/SGD behavior consistent with a simple limiting model.

fits_no_version.finding: Depth-scaled initialization produces nondegenerate forward diffusion limits and, under non-explosivity conditions, finite invertible limiting Jacobians in fully connected identity ResNets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitable depth-dependent initialization preserves signal dependence and avoids exploding Jacobians at initialization in the studied residual architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: For the restricted fully connected architecture with identity inner activation and i.i.d. parameters, the doubly infinite Gaussian-process and neural-tangent kernels are affine.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The studied doubly infinite ResNets reduce to linear-model predictions under weak training and, conditional on additional NTK training assumptions, full gradient-flow training.

record.problems: The paper states that the doubly infinite results are not completely mathematically rigorous and rely partly on heuristic propositions. The MNIST accuracy values are presented in figures without individual numerical values; the experiments report test accuracy rather than training classification error.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and effects of capacity, early stopping and regularization.
Spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction by extra student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depth between plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and identity-shortcut networks; special initialization and Fixup alternatives.
Effects of activation-matched initialization on learning speed and trainable depth in plain networks; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and very deep plain convolutional training.
Loss and curvature dynamics near or above learning-rate stability thresholds, recovery, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply. Initialization-time propagation and expressivity results concern related constructs, and final test accuracy cannot substitute for the training outcomes named by the versions.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; model size and training-duration effects.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Plain versus residual networks' training error across depth, and special initialization or normalization comparisons.
Comparisons of activation-matched, Gaussian, and orthogonal initializations on learning speed or trainable depth.
Training behavior above or near a learning-rate stability threshold and sharpness dynamics.
Batch-normalization comparisons of training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.baseline: Theoretical limiting value corresponding to Bayesian linear regression; 85.36% test accuracy is reported for the kernel-regression reference with added noise variance 1/20.000.
rows.note: The text says there is strong agreement with the limiting theoretical test accuracy, but does not give individual plotted values. This is test accuracy, not training error.
rows.check: Final test accuracy relative to a linear-regression reference cannot establish any version's training outcome. Individual plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text.
